candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Before any concept work begins, we’ll send over some examples we like, although we’re also interested in your own ideas. Please hold off on starting the concepts until we’ve got back to you. Thanks, Tessa

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text:
Attached is an AI-generated draft logo that we made while simply experimenting with chat gpt. It is only inspiration: we still want fresh, original ideas, which is why we posted the proposal. We do, however, like its colours because they fit the look and feel of the Copper Crust truck.

The company is called ‘Copper Crust’, so the logo must not contain the word ‘truck’. The mobile catering truck is only one part of the wider business. Copper Crust will operate that truck, sell food online and may also supply other caterers or kitchens. That broader scope is why the company name excludes ‘truck’, while the existing strapline remains unchanged. Would you be happy to discuss any of this before accepting the offer?

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text:
The graduated orange colour and the lines beside the strapline both work well for us. Of the concepts, we like the 2nd and 6th one; the typeface in the 5th one feels too plain. Our concern with the flame in the 6th one is that someone unfamiliar with our name may not recognise it as an ‘O’, although we do like the treatment.

Could you test every suggested solution: enclosing the flame within an ‘O’, shaping the flame more clearly like an ‘O’, and superimposing it onto an ‘O’?

For logo 6, please also show us how a slightly larger ‘dough’ would look. The strapline could stand out either by outlining every letter with a thin black pencil line or by slightly brightening the orange tones in its lettering. We like the character of the font used for copper crust, particularly the G. We wondered whether a couple of the other letters could gain a little character too, but it would be better to handle revisions one stage at a time because the current font may already be suitable. Thank you—we’re moving in the right direction.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text:
Apologies for the delay. Julian prefers number 7, where the strapline matches the colour of ‘global’ and both use graduated colours.

I would still like the ‘copper crust’ font to have a little more character, reflecting food that will be truly authentic, freshly cooked and full of flavours from around the world. The interesting G shape in both words appeals to me. Could a similar treatment be applied to more letters without overdoing it? Thanks, Tessa

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text:
Thank you for these—we’re nearly there!
1\. For the fifth logo, please reduce the U and H so they match the height of the remaining letters in ‘DOUGH’.
2\. At the top-right of the H in DOUGH, please flip the feature so that it mirrors the top of the U in DOUGH.
3\. Finally, please give the top of the D in DOUGH the same feature used at the top of the B in GLOBAL.

The attached annotated screenshot shows what we mean. Once those revisions are complete, we’ll review it again and hopefully it will retain a ‘clean’ appearance while gaining the character. Many thanks, Tessa

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text:
I mistakenly thought I had already replied! We’d like to proceed with the final version shown above, rev8-11. Thank you.

Am I right that the logo will be provided both with and without the black box, since that background will not suit every use? Will we also receive every colour variant you have shown?

For the main logo, our preference is the top-row treatment from the final version: graduated orange for ‘global’, black for ‘dough’ and graduated orange for the strapline.

We now need the logo guidelines and every relevant file type for online use, social media, the truck and hard-copy materials such as pull-up banners, printed menus and uniforms. Given the large file sizes, how will you share them—through Wetransfer? Thank you, Tessa

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text:
Could you confirm whether the first $240 has been received and whether the second $240 has been released? I’m unsure whether I completed everything required to release the latter amount, so I’ll check again.

Perhaps “guidelines” was not the right term. Earlier, you confirmed that the fixed cost included the brand colors and font, providing what we need to maintain a consistent brand identity. Those details are what I meant rather than a separate guidelines project.

For the colour versions, we only need the three you stated above. Thanks, Tessa

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text:
I’ve only now had a chance to sit down with my laptop and open the delivered files. The colour codes document gives an error, so I’m unable to open it. The jpgs and pdfs work without any problem, but I cannot open the AI, EPS or PSD files. Among the png files, only logo 7 opens correctly; all the others fail to open properly.

I also need to know whether you used an existing font for the logo or created the lettering yourself. If it was custom-made, which font should we use on the website and other materials to complement or match the logo, for example in some headers? Thanks, Tessa

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text:
Thanks for clarifying things. The colour codes document still won’t open for me, so I’ll wait to hear back about the PNG files. If screenshots of what appears when I try opening them would help, I can send those later. And yes, please recommend fonts that would complement the logo.

Thanks,
Tessa

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Thank you. To tick all those boxes and allow us to trademark the logo in due course, could you also confirm in writing that we own the copyright?

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Before proceeding, could you email me a draft or template certificate so I can check whether the wording is sufficient?
